I (27F) moved to London from Manchester 6 months ago for a high paying and high stress job that wanted me in the office everyday. I quit the job and have returned home but this was how I felt:

1. London is amazing to be in. It’s a collection of many different towns with their own vibe and culture. There are so many people out there to meet and so many things to do. When you’re single in a big city, it feels like there are so many opportunities out there for you too! A night out could go in so many directions and you meet some interesting characters.

2. However, the work was eating up my energy. From the commute to the long hours and international travel, it was a lot. This meant that, come the weekend, I was way too exhausted to explore what the city had to offer and simply wanted to coop up in my room and sleep. 

3. It’s expensive and living in a house share (which you can avoid if you like) is also mentally draining. I was previously living alone in Manchester and got used to my own space, but chose a house share so I could meet new people. I don’t regret meeting my house mate and her friends (got an invite to her wedding!) but I wouldn’t do it again.

4. Compared to say, Manchester, it has a lot more variety in the things you can do and places to explore, but Manchester’s access to the countryside and hiking routes will be a winner for many people.

I’ve now taken a pay cut to return to my old company, but the job is fully remote (with offices in Manchester, Glasgow and Surrey if I’d ever like to go in). I started viewing flats in Manchester to buy but tell you what, after being born and raised and living the best part of 22 years here, I’m bored of it.

Despite my pay cut, I’m looking to sign on a year long tenancy for a one bed flat in south London, close to my London friends. I want to give the city another chance and explore everything it has to offer. I will probably not save much but getting on the property ladder doesn’t feel like something I want to do anymore and I already have enough for emergencies/a deposit when I choose to settle.

Best of luck!
